newsitem.title: DUBAI: GM Mideast car sales up 50 pct in four months.
newsitem.headline: GM Mideast car sales up 50 pct in four months.

text.p: Middle East sales of General Motors passenger cars rose nearly 50 percent in the past four months, a statement from the GM regional office said on Tuesday.
From July to October sales of GM cars rose 48 percent over the same period in 1995, led by stronger sales of the Chevrolet Cavalier. It did not give a figure for total units sold.

"Sales of the Cavalier so far this year are up 315 percent on the first ten months of last year," GM Middle East director Alan Batey said, but added the figure was slightly distorted as Cavalier was not fully available in the market in early-1995.
"Nevertheless it is a very positive indication that the Cavalier...is making serious inroads into Japanese domination of the small car market."

The Chevrolet Caprice posted its highest monthly sales for more than two years and Cadillac sales rose 15 percent in the four-month period, GM said. Cadillac results in the past two months were the best in nearly three years.
"It would be too early to describe this as a major upward trend in the automobile market which has been badly hit over recent years, but it is very encouraging," Batey said.
The Gulf car market has taken a knock in recent years as lower oil prices until early 1996 put a brake on state spending and dragged down consumer confidence.
